name: Nobitex
rootCause: The Iran-based Nobitex cryptocurrency exchange suffered a $90 million hack, and the attacker has also promised to imminently release data and source code from the platform. The hacking group appears to have burned the crypto assets, effectively destroying them rather than taking them for their own profits. Gonjeshke Darande (also "Predatory Sparrow"), a hacking group with links to Israel, claimed responsibility for the theft, accusing the platform of serving as a "key regime tool" to finance terror and violate sanctions.

descriptions.text: The Iran-based Nobitex cryptocurrency exchange suffered a $90 million hack, and the attacker has also promised to imminently release data and source code from the platform. The hacking group appears to have burned the crypto assets, effectively destroying them rather than taking them for their own profits. Gonjeshke Darande (also "Predatory Sparrow"), a hacking group with links to Israel, claimed responsibility for the theft, accusing the platform of serving as a "key regime tool" to finance terror and violate sanctions.

On 2025-06-18, Iranian cryptocurrency exchange Nobitex disclosed unauthorized access to internal systems and portions of its hot-wallet infrastructure. Attackers linked to the hacktivist group Gonjeshke Darande drained assets across multiple blockchains and routed many transfers to politically themed vanity addresses, turning the incident into a destructive geopolitical cyber operation rather than a conventional profit-seeking exchange theft. Nobitex confirmed unauthorized access to internal systems and hot wallets but did not publish a full technical postmortem identifying the exact intrusion path. The Iran-based Nobitex cryptocurrency exchange suffered a $90 million hack, and the attacker has also promised to imminently release data and source code from the platform. The hacking group appears to have burned the crypto assets, effectively destroying them rather than taking them for their own profits. Gonjeshke Darande (also "Predatory Sparrow"), a hacking group with links to Israel, claimed responsibility for the theft, accusing the platform of serving as a "key regime tool" to finance terror and violate sanctions. The cyberattack comes shortly after Israel launched air strikes on Iran.
